editorial:
Imagine a guy whose whole life is based on hate and narrow rules, only to have it all flip upside down in the weirdest way possible. You meet Jan, a young neo-Nazi who thinks he has everything figured out. His world is small and angry, but he feels safe in it. Everything changes when he has to run from the cops and accidentally hides out in an Asian strip club. It is a wild, awkward setup that takes a very hateful person and throws him into a world he was taught to despise, creating a comedy that is both cringey and surprisingly heart-warming.

What really works here is how the movie handles Jan's slow realization that his beliefs are total nonsense. The acting is great because it doesn't make him a cartoon; he feels like a real, confused kid. The pacing is quick, though some scenes might feel a bit too strange for some. If you like dark humor and stories about people changing for the better, you will love this.
endingExplained: By the end, Jan completely rejects his hateful skinhead friends and the ideology he grew up with. After finding genuine connection and love in the strip club, he realizes that the people he was told to hate are actually the only ones who treat him with kindness. He chooses a life of openness over hate, leaving his old gang behind for good. It wraps up with Jan finally feeling free and happy as a changed man.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies about unlikely friendships.
